story.title: ICC Finds Former CAR Militia Commander Guilty of Crimes Against Humanity
story.summary: The International Criminal Court has found Mahamat Said Abdel Kani, a former militia commander in the Central African Republic, guilty of crimes against humanity. He was determined to have overseen torture and abuse of prisoners at a detention facility in Bangui. The court's ruling highlights the brutal tactics employed during his leadership of a feared prison unit.

explore_lenses.label: Why does this conviction matter for CAR?
explore_lenses.title: It reaches the Séléka side of the conflict
explore_lenses.summary: The verdict is significant because the ICC’s CAR II investigation covers alleged crimes by groups linked to both the predominantly Muslim Séléka coalition and the mainly Christian anti-Balaka militias. Reuters reports that Said is the first Séléka member convicted by the court, extending individual accountability beyond the anti-Balaka cases.

claims.text: The CAR’s transitional authorities referred alleged crimes committed since August 1, 2012 to the ICC in May 2014; the ICC’s investigation has focused on alleged crimes by groups linked to both Séléka and anti-Balaka forces.
Reuters reports that Said is the first Séléka member convicted by the ICC, after the court convicted two anti-Balaka leaders.
The ruling concerns one defendant and does not amount to a judicial finding about responsibility for all violence during CAR’s conflict.

The ruling concerns one defendant and does not amount to a judicial finding about responsibility for all violence during CAR’s conflict.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The verdict’s broader effect on accountability in CAR will depend on outcomes in other cases and investigations, which this judgment does not decide.

explore_lenses.label: How did the case reach a verdict?
explore_lenses.title: A long ICC process followed the 2013 abuses
explore_lenses.summary: The case moved from a sealed 2019 arrest warrant to Said’s surrender in 2021, a trial beginning in 2022, and closing arguments in late 2025. The defense denied the charges, while judges ultimately found the prosecution had proved four crimes against humanity.

claims.text: The ICC issued Said’s arrest warrant under seal on January 7, 2019; he was surrendered to the court on January 24, 2021, and his trial opened on September 26, 2022.
The prosecution concluded its evidence in November 2024 after calling 58 witnesses; the defense concluded its case on September 2, 2025, and closing statements were heard on November 25-26, 2025.
Said denied all charges; his defense previously characterized the prosecution’s account as biased and incomplete.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after the guilty verdict?
explore_lenses.title: Sentencing and a possible appeal remain
explore_lenses.summary: The conviction does not yet establish Said’s prison term. A separate ICC hearing is expected to determine sentence, and the Rome Statute provides routes to appeal convictions and sentences.

claims.text: Judges convicted Said on four crimes-against-humanity counts, including persecution and torture, while dismissing several war-crimes charges after finding the armed conflict had ended when some alleged conduct occurred.
A separate hearing will determine Said’s sentence.
The Rome Statute permits the convicted person or prosecutor to appeal a conviction or sentence on specified grounds, so the verdict may not be final until appeal rights are resolved or expire.
Forecast: the next substantive public development is likely to be sentencing proceedings, because Reuters reports that sentencing has been deferred to a separate hearing.

story_report.summary: International Criminal Court judges convicted former Central African Republic militia commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani of four counts of crimes against humanity, including persecution and torture, for overseeing the torture and abuse of prisoners at a detention facility in the country. The court dismissed several war-crimes charges after finding that the armed conflict had ended when some alleged conduct occurred. A separate hearing will determine his sentence; no date or proposed penalty had been reported as of Sept. 23, 2026.

sections.heading: CAR Referral and ICC Investigation
sections.body: CAR’s transitional authorities referred alleged crimes committed from Aug. 1, 2012, to the ICC in May 2014. The court’s investigation has examined alleged crimes by groups linked to both the Séléka and anti-Balaka forces. Reuters reported that Said is the first Séléka member convicted by the ICC, following convictions of two anti-Balaka leaders.

sections.heading: Said Defense and Trial Timeline
sections.body: The ICC issued Said’s arrest warrant under seal in January 2019, and he was surrendered to the court in January 2021. His trial began in September 2022; prosecutors finished presenting evidence in November 2024 after calling 58 witnesses, while the defense concluded in September 2025 and closing statements followed in November. Said denied all charges, and his defense had described the prosecution’s account as biased and incomplete.

sections.heading: Said Sentencing and Appeal Rights
sections.body: Sentencing proceedings are the likely next substantive public stage because the court deferred punishment to a separate hearing. Under the Rome Statute, either the convicted person or the prosecutor may appeal a conviction or sentence on specified grounds. The verdict therefore may not become final until appeal rights are resolved or expire.

unresolved.text: Public reporting available on Sept. 23 did not provide the full reasoning in the written trial judgment.
No sentencing date, proposed penalty or appeal filing was reported in the consulted sources as of Sept. 23, 2026.
The judgment concerns Said alone and does not determine responsibility for all violence during CAR’s conflict; its wider accountability effect depends on other cases and investigations.

related_stories.title: Mass Shooting at South African House Party Claims 11 Lives
related_stories.summary: A mass shooting at a house party in South Africa resulted in the deaths of at least 11 people, including a pregnant woman. The attack involved three gunmen who forced the victims into a single room before opening fire, leaving only two survivors. Police are currently searching for the attackers.

related_stories.title: Kyiv Struck by Russian Drones Ahead of Zelenskyy's UN Address
related_stories.summary: On Wednesday, Kyiv was targeted by Russian drone strikes, resulting in two fatalities and 23 injuries. The attacks occurred just hours before Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was scheduled to address the United Nations General Assembly. The strikes hit various locations, including railway infrastructure and fuel stations, amid ongoing tensions in the region.

related_stories.title: Morocco Holds Parliamentary Elections Amid Youth Discontent and Economic Concerns
related_stories.summary: Moroccans are voting in parliamentary elections today, with significant concerns regarding the cost of living, jobs, and inequality. Many voters, particularly the youth, express deep distrust in political parties, reflecting a broader discontent that has been evident since youth-led demonstrations a year ago. The elections are seen as a crucial test of citizens' faith in the political process as the country prepares for the 2030 World Cup.
